note.question: How do overconfident customers change congestion, optimal admission prices, information disclosure, revenue, and welfare in observable and unobservable queues?
note.overview: Customers play strategic join/balk queueing games under biased service-time beliefs, and the manager prices and chooses information anticipating the equilibrium.
